narrativeReportMd:
# Medication R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps the same `Medication` resource identity, but local Medication content changed enough that breaking changes are found. The highest-impact changes are top-level and nested element renames/removals (`manufacturer`, `form`, `amount`, `batch`), choice/datatype rewrites for ingredients, and new R6-only references that cannot round-trip to base R4.

## Scope
This report compares the base R4 `Medication` StructureDefinition from `hl7.fhir.r4.core#4.0.1` with the R6 ballot `Medication` StructureDefinition from `hl7.fhir.r6.core#6.0.0-ballot4`. It covers local Medication elements, local bindings, related Medication value sets/code systems inspected from the two packages, and the directly relevant R6 `CodeableReference` datatype. Inherited `DomainResource`, `Resource`, `Element`, `Extension`, and datatype-wide changes are excluded from findings.

## Main migration themes
Most R4→R6 breaks are validation and serializer breaks caused by element names and shapes changing: `form`→`doseForm`, `batch`→`instance`, `amount`→`packageSize`, `ingredient.item[x]`→`ingredient.item` as `CodeableReference`, and `ingredient.strength`→`strength[x]`. R6 also adds richer product-definition and ingredient-role data that cannot be represented in base R4 without extensions or external mapping.

## Highest-impact findings
The hard instance-breaking findings are the removed/renamed fields and ingredient representation changes. `Medication.amount` to `packageSize`, `ingredient.item` to `CodeableReference`, and `ingredient.strength[x]` carry the largest R6→R4 loss risk because R6 can express information that R4 has no equivalent place or type for.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important where the apparent mapping is not semantically exact: manufacturer versus marketing authorization holder, package amount versus package-size decomposition, R6 ingredient strength quantities/codes, and status semantics shifting from medication availability to record currentness.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been less disruptive if R6 had retained deprecated R4 elements during a transition. The most avoidable-looking pure rename is `form`→`doseForm`; the richer modeling changes are more justified but still could have been introduced additively.

## Follow-up analysis
Base-artifact changes, `CodeableReference`, R6 product-definition resources, and terminology expansions should be reviewed separately before defining a production migration playbook.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `Medication` preserves identity but has multiple hard local instance breaks. The top concerns are local element renames/removals, ingredient choice/type rewrites, and R6-only package/product-definition data that cannot round-trip to R4. Confidence is high for structural findings; terminology and rationale confidence would improve with official diffs and expansions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a field-level transform, not a version-label update. Rename or restructure top-level fields (`form`, `manufacturer`, `amount`, `batch`), rewrite ingredient representation (`item[x]` to `CodeableReference`, `strength` to `strength[x]`), and define explicit downgrade extensions for R6-only `role`, `definition`, `packageSize`, `instance.identifier`, `SubstanceDefinition`, and non-Ratio strengths.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local structural changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for semantic rationale and terminology impact because no official diff/change note or terminology-server expansion was used, and the R6 input is a ballot build.

findings.title: Medication.manufacturer was replaced by marketingAuthorizationHolder with narrower semantics

semanticText.definition: Describes the details of the manufacturer of the medication product. This is not intended to represent the distributor of a medication product.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `Medication.manufacturer` as a summary Organization reference for the manufacturing organization.

semanticText.short: Organization that has authorization to market medication
semanticText.definition: The company or other legal entity that has authorization, from the appropriate drug regulatory authority, to market a medicine in one or more jurisdictions. The MAH may manufacture the product and may also contract the manufacturing of the product.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes the `manufacturer` element and introduces `marketingAuthorizationHolder`, still an Organization reference but with legal/regulatory-holder semantics rather than a direct manufacturing-party meaning.

facts.note: R4 path is absent from the R6 snapshot and differential.
R6 path has the same cardinality and target type but a different definition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The elements match structurally (`0..1`, `Reference(Organization)`, summary=true) and occupy the same top-level slot, but their definitions are not equivalent: a marketing authorization holder may be the manufacturer or may contract manufacturing to another organization.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format break for R4→R6: `manufacturer` is not an R6 `Medication` element, so strict parsers and validators reject old instances that carry it. It is also a semantic migration risk because copying manufacturer into `marketingAuthorizationHolder` can be clinically or regulatorily wrong when the manufacturer and authorization holder differ.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The field can drive labeling, regulatory, formulary, and product-identification logic. Misidentifying the legal authorization holder as the manufacturer, or vice versa, can affect downstream business rules.

justification.inferredGoal: Align Medication with regulatory product modeling where the legal marketing authorization holder is distinct from physical manufacturing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `manufacturer` as a deprecated or clarified Organization role and add optional `marketingAuthorizationHolder` for the regulatory holder role.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Modeling the marketing authorization holder is a reasonable R6 regulatory-product goal, but it did not require removing the R4 manufacturer role. Because manufacturer and MAH are not semantically equivalent, forcing a rename can create incorrect migrations when the physical manufacturer differs from the legal holder. A less-breaking base design could preserve old instances while adding the more precise R6 role, so the removal looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would keep `Medication.manufacturer` valid, update its definition if needed to distinguish it from distributor and MAH, and add `Medication.marketingAuthorizationHolder` as the new regulatory role. Profiles or invariants could warn about conflicting or duplicate Organizations. This is not just migration guidance: it would allow unconverted R4 instances to remain valid in base R6 while still supporting the R6 MAH concept.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains an older role name and requires guidance for manufacturer/MAH consistency, but avoids invalidating R4 instances with moderate long-term cost.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Medication.manufacturer` as `0..1 Reference(Organization)` and summary=true.
R6 defines `Medication.marketingAuthorizationHolder` as `0..1 Reference(Organization)` and summary=true.
evidence.quote: Organization that has authorization to market medication

evidence.detail: No R6 element with id/path `Medication.manufacturer` is present.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are fragments. A lossless migration requires deciding whether the R4 Organization really represents the legal marketing authorization holder.

findings.narrativeMd: `Medication.manufacturer` did not survive as the same element in R6. The closest R6 element is `marketingAuthorizationHolder`, but this is not just a spelling change: the R6 text says the MAH may manufacture the product or contract manufacturing out. Systems that treated `manufacturer` as the actual maker should not blindly rename the element without checking their source semantics.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `manufacturer` can be old-valid/new-invalid because R6 has no such element. An R6 instance containing `marketingAuthorizationHolder` is not directly R4-representable without using an extension or mapping it into `manufacturer` with possible semantic loss. Generated R4 and R6 model classes will expose different property names, and business rules keyed on manufacturer need review.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory uses of `manufacturer`. If it denotes the legal MAH, rename to `marketingAuthorizationHolder`. If it denotes the physical manufacturer, preserve it in an extension or another product-definition resource rather than mapping it as MAH. Test cases should include a product where the manufacturer and MAH are different.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been less disruptive by retaining `manufacturer` and adding `marketingAuthorizationHolder` as a new, more precise optional element. That alternative would keep R4 instances valid but would leave implementers with two related roles to reconcile.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The structural match is clear, but the semantic match is intentionally only medium-confidence because the old and new role definitions differ.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Medication.manufacturer` is not present in the R6 base resource, and the nearest R6 slot, `marketingAuthorizationHolder`, is a different legal/regulatory role. An old instance with `manufacturer` is rejected by an R6 validator unless transformed, and a blind transform can be wrong when the physical manufacturer differs from the marketing authorization holder. Because the affected resource is mature trial-use medication content and the migration requires semantic judgment, this deserves renewed standards/design attention.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=Medication.manufacturer]: `0..1 Reference(Organization)`, summary=true, short `Manufacturer of the item`.
R6 StructureDefinition has `Medication.marketingAuthorizationHolder` as `0..1 Reference(Organization)` and no `Medication.manufacturer` element.
R6 `marketingAuthorizationHolder` definition says the MAH may manufacture the product or contract manufacturing to other organizations.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 3 and trial-use status create a meaningful stability expectation for common Medication exchange, though not a normative one; that pushes a semantically non-equivalent rename toward Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances carrying `manufacturer` have an element unknown to base R6, and generated models/business rules also move from a manufacturer property to a MAH property.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have retained optional `manufacturer` while adding optional `marketingAuthorizationHolder`, or clarified `manufacturer` while distinguishing it from MAH. The tradeoff is two related organization roles and consistency guidance, but that is lower cost than forcing a semantically unsafe rename.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as a hard break with a real less-breaking base design.

findings.title: Medication.form was renamed to doseForm

binding.description: A coded concept defining the form of a medication.

semanticText.definition: Describes the form of the item. Powder; tablets; capsule.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented the medication dose form in `Medication.form`.

newState.summary: Optional CodeableConcept doseForm element with the same cardinality, type, binding, and descriptive text.

binding.description: A coded concept defining the form of a medication.

semanticText.definition: Describes the form of the item. Powder; tablets; capsule.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `Medication.doseForm` for the same computable definition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 elements have identical cardinality, type, binding, short text, definition, and comment; only the path/name changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR JSON/XML element names are normative. `form` is unknown in R6 and `doseForm` is unknown in R4, even though the value content can be transformed losslessly in ordinary cases.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dose form affects prescribing, dispensing, and administration interpretation. The primary risk is failed parsing or omitted data during migration rather than changed clinical meaning.

justification.inferredGoal: Use a more explicit element name for medication dose form.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `form` as the base element name and clarify that it means dose form, or retain it as a deprecated alias if `doseForm` is added.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 name is clearer, but the cardinality, type, binding, and descriptive text otherwise match the R4 element. This is a pure local wire rename, so preserving the R4 name with clearer wording would have met the apparent goal with much less breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design could leave `Medication.form` as `0..1 CodeableConcept` and revise the short/definition to say dose form. If R6 also wanted the `doseForm` spelling, `form` could remain a deprecated alias with an invariant prohibiting both. The first option preserves all R4 instances without adding duplicate representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a shorter legacy name or, if both names exist, needs duplicate-field conflict rules; avoiding the rename has low compatibility cost.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Medication.form` as `0..1 CodeableConcept` with example binding to medication-form-codes.
R6 defines `Medication.doseForm` as `0..1 CodeableConcept` with the same example binding and definition.
No R6 element with id/path `Medication.form` is present.

examples.examplesMd: This rename is normally mechanically transformable: `form` ↔ `doseForm`.

findings.narrativeMd: `Medication.form` was renamed to `Medication.doseForm`. This is structurally simple but still hard-breaking for instances and generated code because FHIR serializers do not treat element aliases as interchangeable.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `form` is invalid against the R6 StructureDefinition due to an unknown element. An R6 instance with `doseForm` is invalid against R4 for the same reason. The underlying CodeableConcept can usually be carried across without loss, subject to terminology differences in the example value set.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `form` to `doseForm` for R4→R6 and reverse the rename for R6→R4. Update generated model properties, FHIRPath expressions, mapping rules, search/extraction logic, and tests that refer to `Medication.form`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the element definition and binding are otherwise unchanged, preserving `form` would have been the least disruptive design. If both names existed, a constraint could have prohibited sending both simultaneously while allowing legacy data to validate.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Medication.form` became `Medication.doseForm` with the same cardinality, datatype, example binding, and descriptive meaning. The data migration is usually mechanical, but the base wire name changed, so unconverted R4 instances and generated property references fail. For FMM 3 trial-use content, a pure clarity rename with a low-cost compatible design is disproportionate enough to revisit.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot.element[id=Medication.form]: `0..1 CodeableConcept`, example binding to `medication-form-codes`, definition `Describes the form of the item`.
R6 snapshot.element[id=Medication.doseForm]: `0..1 CodeableConcept`, same example binding and same definition text.
No R6 snapshot element with id/path `Medication.form` is present.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not forbid renames, but this is a mature central resource and the change appears to be naming clarity rather than a necessary model correction.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: `form` is not a base R6 Medication element; R6 `doseForm` is also not a base R4 Medication element.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. Keeping `form` and clarifying its definition to mean dose form would preserve R4 instances without duplicate data. A deprecated alias would also work but would need a mutual-exclusion rule if both names were allowed.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly flags the hard rename and a Yes alternative, but the practical data-loss risk is narrow because values can be transformed losslessly.

findings.title: Medication.amount was replaced by packageSize.numberOfItems and packageSize.amountPerItem

oldState.summary: Optional top-level Ratio for amount of drug in package.

semanticText.definition: Specific amount of the drug in the packaged product.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used one top-level `Ratio` to clarify package amount, for example 3 mL or 10 mL for a packaged product.

newState.summary: Optional packageSize backbone with numberOfItems and amountPerItem children.

semanticText.short: When the code does not specify the package size, this backbone element can be used to specify the overall amount of medication in the package
semanticText.definition: When the code does not specify the package size, this backbone element can be used to specify the overall amount of medication in the package.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses a nested `packageSize` backbone with optional `numberOfItems` (`SimpleQuantity`) and `amountPerItem` (`Ratio`) to distinguish package count from per-item amount.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both old and new content describe package amount/size, but R6 decomposes the concept into count and amount-per-item, so the correspondence is not a direct rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `amount` are rejected by R6 because the element is removed. R6 instances can contain two package-size facts that do not fit into R4's single `Ratio` without a policy decision, especially when `numberOfItems` and `amountPerItem` are both present.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect package quantity mapping can affect dispensing quantity, inventory, and medication identification.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent package size more accurately by separating number of items from amount per item.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `packageSize` while retaining deprecated `amount` for simple package-amount cases.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 package-size backbone addresses a real ambiguity in the R4 single `Ratio`, especially where package count and per-item amount are distinct. A less-breaking base design exists, but retaining `amount` beside `packageSize` would leave duplicate ways to state package size and require conflict rules for operationally important quantity data. Those material tradeoffs make the breaking redesign probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would keep `Medication.amount` valid and add `Medication.packageSize` for richer R6 content. Simple R4 amounts would continue to validate, while new R6 instances could use `numberOfItems` and `amountPerItem`. The cost is persistent same-resource duplication: validators and applications would need rules for cases where both `amount` and `packageSize` are populated or disagree, and the old field would still not represent all R6 package-size facts.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 package amounts, but creates overlapping package-size representations and cannot fully express R6 number-of-items plus amount-per-item semantics in the old `Ratio`.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Medication.amount` as `0..1 Ratio` and summary=true.
R6 defines a `0..1` `packageSize` backbone and no `Medication.amount` element.
evidence.quote: When the code does not specify the package size...

evidence.detail: R6 adds `numberOfItems` as `0..1 Quantity` profiled to SimpleQuantity.
R6 adds `amountPerItem` as `0..1 Ratio`.

examples.examplesMd: The R4→R6 example maps a simple package amount into `amountPerItem`; that may not be correct for every historical use of `amount`.

findings.narrativeMd: The old top-level package amount was replaced by a richer package-size backbone. This is not just a rename because R6 can represent a number of items and an amount per item separately, while R4 had only one `Ratio` slot.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data with `amount` is old-valid/new-invalid. R6 data with `packageSize` is not cleanly R4-representable if it uses `numberOfItems` or both children. Strict code generators will also change from a `Ratio amount` property to a nested `PackageSize` component.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create explicit mapping rules for known package patterns. Simple R4 `amount` values may map to `packageSize.amountPerItem`, but package-count data should populate `numberOfItems`. For R6→R4, preserve `packageSize` in extensions or product-definition resources if both children are clinically or operationally meaningful.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The improved model could have been introduced additively while retaining `amount` as deprecated. That would avoid immediate validation breaks but leave overlapping ways to say package size.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed for any migration rule that tries to infer whether an R4 `amount` is per item, per package, or total package content.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 used one `Medication.amount` Ratio for package amount; R6 replaces it with a `packageSize` backbone that can distinguish item count from amount per item. This is a hard wire/codegen break for old data and can be lossy in reverse, but the R6 goal addresses a real ambiguity in the R4 shape. Retaining the old field would create overlapping package-size representations for operational quantity data, so the break appears proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot.element[id=Medication.amount]: `0..1 Ratio`, summary=true, short `Amount of drug in package`.
R6 snapshot.element[id=Medication.packageSize]: `0..1 BackboneElement`, summary=true, with invariant `med-1` requiring `numberOfItems` or `amountPerItem`.
R6 `Medication.packageSize.numberOfItems` is `0..1 SimpleQuantity`; `Medication.packageSize.amountPerItem` is `0..1 Ratio`; no R6 `Medication.amount` element is present.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises the bar for disrupting package quantity exchange, but it also leaves room for a proportionate redesign that fixes an ambiguous mature element.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `amount` is unknown in R6 and must be restructured; R6 `packageSize` values, especially count plus amount-per-item, do not collapse cleanly to the single R4 Ratio.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have kept deprecated `amount` and added `packageSize`, preserving simple R4 instances. The tradeoff is duplicate/conflicting ways to state package size and no full representation of R6 count-plus-per-item semantics in the old field.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly identifies a high-impact hard break and only a partial less-breaking alternative.

findings.title: Ingredient item changed from item[x] choice to CodeableReference and added SubstanceDefinition target

oldState.summary: Required choice element with CodeableConcept or Reference(Substance|Medication).

semanticText.definition: The actual ingredient - either a substance (simple ingredient) or another medication of a medication.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 serialized the choice as `itemCodeableConcept` or `itemReference`.

newState.summary: Required CodeableReference to concept or Reference(Substance|SubstanceDefinition|Medication) with example medication-codes binding.

semanticText.short: The specific substance or medication that is the ingredient
semanticText.definition: The ingredient (substance or medication) that the ingredient.strength relates to.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 serializes the ingredient as a `CodeableReference` object with `concept` and/or `reference` children and allows a `SubstanceDefinition` reference.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element remains required and expresses the same ingredient identity concept, but R6 adopts the `CodeableReference` datatype instead of the R4 choice-element wire representation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard serialization and codegen break. R4 uses choice-suffixed JSON names such as `itemCodeableConcept`; R6 expects `item` containing a `CodeableReference`. R6 also permits references to `SubstanceDefinition`, a resource not present in R4, so some valid R6 ingredients cannot be represented as valid R4 `Medication.ingredient.itemReference` targets.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ingredient identity affects clinical interpretation, compounding, and decision support. A missed concept/reference conversion can drop the active ingredient.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt the newer CodeableReference pattern so an ingredient can be represented uniformly as either a coded concept or a resource reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 `ingredient.item[x]` as a deprecated compatibility path while adding or preferring the R6 CodeableReference representation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using `CodeableReference` for ingredient identity is a coherent R6 modeling goal and aligns with broader R6 concept-or-reference patterns. A less-breaking base design could keep the old choice elements valid, but for a required ingredient field it would create competing representations for clinically important identity data and complicate validation, generated models, and interoperability. Those tradeoffs make the alternative only partial.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would keep `itemCodeableConcept` and `itemReference` valid, possibly widen `itemReference` to include `SubstanceDefinition`, and add `item` CodeableReference as the preferred R6 form. That would preserve common R4 instances, but systems would need precedence and consistency rules when old and new ingredient identities are both present, and the R4 choice shape cannot natively represent a single CodeableReference containing both `concept` and `reference`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old ingredient identities, but creates duplicate required ingredient representations and cannot fully match CodeableReference cases that carry both concept and reference.

evidence.detail: R4 requires `item[x]` with CodeableConcept or Reference(Substance, Medication).
R6 requires `item` with CodeableReference and target profiles Substance, SubstanceDefinition, Medication.
R6 CodeableReference has `concept` and `reference` children.
`SubstanceDefinition` is not present as an R4 core StructureDefinition.

examples.examplesMd: R4 `itemCodeableConcept` maps naturally to R6 `item.concept`; R4 `itemReference` maps to R6 `item.reference` only when the target remains valid in R6/R4.

findings.narrativeMd: The required ingredient identity element changed from a choice element to `CodeableReference`. Every R4 ingredient uses the old choice naming, so migrations must rewrite the JSON/XML shape even when the underlying concept or reference is unchanged.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `itemCodeableConcept` and `itemReference` are unknown in R6. R6 `item.concept` and `item.reference` are not R4 element names. R6 references to `SubstanceDefinition` are additionally outside the R4 target domain, so they cannot be represented as valid R4 Medication ingredient references without an extension or resource-specific transformation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform `itemCodeableConcept` to `item.concept` and `itemReference` to `item.reference`. Add tests for both forms and for `SubstanceDefinition` references. For R6→R4, map `Substance` and `Medication` references back to `itemReference`, concepts to `itemCodeableConcept`, and preserve `SubstanceDefinition` references in extensions or a separate migration artifact.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 approach is cleaner for new implementations but breaks a required R4 element. A transitional design with both `item[x]` and `item` would have been more compatible, though it would burden implementations with duplicate representations.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required ingredient identity changed from R4 choice serialization (`itemCodeableConcept` or `itemReference`) to an R6 `CodeableReference` object, and R6 also allows `SubstanceDefinition`. This is a real serializer/codegen break on clinically important content, but the R6 pattern is coherent for concept-or-reference modeling. Keeping the old choice beside `CodeableReference` would duplicate a required ingredient identity and require precedence rules, so the break is probably acceptable.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot.element[id=Medication.ingredient.item[x]]: `1..1` choice of `CodeableConcept` or `Reference(Substance|Medication)`.
R6 snapshot.element[id=Medication.ingredient.item]: `1..1 CodeableReference` targeting `Substance`, `SubstanceDefinition`, or `Medication`.
`SubstanceDefinition` is absent from the R4 core package and present in the R6 core package.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes this central ingredient path important, but the maturity level still permits a well-justified model-wide datatype modernization.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 choice-suffixed names are not R6 element names; reverse conversion can also lose `SubstanceDefinition` references or a CodeableReference that carries both concept and reference.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have retained `item[x]` as deprecated compatibility fields while adding `item` CodeableReference, but that would create duplicate required ingredient identity representations and difficult consistency rules.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's hard-break impact and Partial alternative assessment match the independent path-level assessment.

findings.title: Ingredient strength changed from Ratio to strength[x] with Ratio, CodeableConcept, or Quantity

semanticText.definition: Specifies how many (or how much) of the items there are in this Medication. For example, 250 mg per tablet.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 serialized strength as a single `strength` Ratio property.

newState.summary: Optional choice element allowing Ratio, CodeableConcept, or Quantity, with preferred binding for coded strengths.

binding.description: A coded concept defining the strength of an ingredient.

semanticText.definition: Specifies how many (or how much) of the items there are in this Medication... but can also be expressed a quantity when the denominator is assumed to be 1 tablet.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps Ratio as one option but changes the wire name to `strengthRatio` and adds `strengthCodeableConcept` and `strengthQuantity`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old Ratio semantics are retained as one R6 choice type, but the choice conversion changes serialization and expands the value domain.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Even an R4 Ratio strength must be renamed to `strengthRatio` to validate in R6. R6 `strengthQuantity` and `strengthCodeableConcept` values cannot be represented in R4's `Ratio` field without lossy inference or extensions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ingredient strength is clinically important; a failed or lossy conversion can change dose interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Support ingredient strengths that are naturally coded or simple quantities and clarify denominator assumptions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `strength` as Ratio and add separate optional coded or quantity strength fields instead of converting the existing path into `strength[x]`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting quantity and coded strengths is a reasonable R6 clinical-modeling improvement, and the R6 choice form is a clean way to express one logical strength with several datatypes. A compatible design could have kept the old Ratio path, but it would be less regular than a FHIR choice and would need strong rules to prevent conflicting strength representations. Because ingredient strength is safety-relevant, those tradeoffs are material.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would retain `Medication.ingredient.strength` as `0..1 Ratio` and add distinct optional elements for coded or simple-quantity strength, with an invariant that only one strength representation may be present. This preserves unconverted R4 Ratio instances but does not give the same tidy `strength[x]` model and risks long-lived ambiguity if deprecated and new strength fields are both supported.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 Ratio strengths, but leaves multiple mutually exclusive strength fields and possible conflict rules for safety-relevant strength data.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `strength` as `0..1 Ratio`.
R6 defines `strength[x]` as `0..1` with Ratio, CodeableConcept, or Quantity.
R6 adds a preferred binding to medication-ingredientstrength for coded strengths.
R6 ingredient strength CodeSystem contains `qs` and `trace` codes.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 Ratio can usually be preserved as R6 `strengthRatio`; new R6 coded/quantity strengths need a separate R4 preservation strategy.

findings.narrativeMd: `ingredient.strength` became a choice element. This widens the clinical value domain but makes old Ratio-valued instances fail unless the element name is changed to `strengthRatio`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `strength` is not an R6 field name; R6 expects a choice-suffixed name. R6 `strengthQuantity` and `strengthCodeableConcept` are not valid R4 Medication elements and cannot always be converted to a Ratio without assumptions about denominator and units.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, rewrite Ratio values from `strength` to `strengthRatio`. For R6→R4, map `strengthRatio` back to `strength` but retain `strengthQuantity` and `strengthCodeableConcept` in extensions or require manual conversion rules. Test dose-calculation and display logic with Ratio, Quantity, and coded strength examples.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: R6's expanded choice is clinically useful, but the same goal could have been achieved by adding optional elements while preserving the old Ratio name. The cleaner R6 representation trades off against strict instance compatibility.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `ingredient.strength` was a Ratio named `strength`; R6 turns the path into `strength[x]`, so even the retained Ratio value now serializes as `strengthRatio`, while coded and Quantity strengths are added. This breaks old instances and generated code, and reverse migration can be lossy for the new types. The added choices address real strength-expression cases such as simple quantities and coded `trace`/`qs`, and a compatible design would leave multiple mutually exclusive strength fields, so the redesign looks proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot.element[id=Medication.ingredient.strength]: `0..1 Ratio`.
R6 snapshot.element[id=Medication.ingredient.strength[x]]: `0..1` choice of `Ratio`, `CodeableConcept`, or `Quantity` with preferred binding to `medication-ingredientstrength`.
R6 CodeSystem `medication-ingredientstrength` includes `qs` and `trace` codes.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use increases concern because ingredient strength is safety-relevant, but the R6 widening has a plausible clinical modeling rationale.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `strength` is not the R6 choice-suffixed name; R6 `strengthCodeableConcept` and `strengthQuantity` have no base R4 equivalent.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could keep `strength` as Ratio and add separate coded/quantity elements with an invariant allowing only one, but that would be less regular than a FHIR choice and would create conflict handling for safety-relevant strength data.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as a hard serialization/type break with only a partial less-breaking alternative.

findings.title: Medication.ingredient.role was added and is not representable in base R4 Medication

oldState.summary: No base R4 element for ingredient role.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had `ingredient.isActive` but no separate coded role/classification for the ingredient.

newState.summary: Optional CodeableConcept ingredient role with example binding to v3 RoleClassIngredientEntity.

semanticText.short: A code that defines the type of ingredient, active, base, etc.
semanticText.definition: Indication of whether this ingredient affects the therapeutic action of the drug.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can carry a coded ingredient role in addition to the boolean `isActive`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This optional addition does not invalidate R4 instances moving to R6. It does create round-trip loss for R6 instances because R4 has no base element to carry the coded role except by extension or by reducing it to `isActive`, which loses detail.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ingredient role can distinguish active, base, excipient, or similar roles. Losing it can alter product interpretation in detailed medication knowledge workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Provide more detail about the type or therapeutic role of an ingredient.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; `ingredient.role` is an optional R6 addition and does not invalidate R4 Medication instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding an optional coded ingredient role is the normal forward-compatible way to expand the base resource. It preserves R4-to-R6 validity and only creates a downgrade concern when populated R6 role data must be represented in R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed to preserve R4 instances because the element is optional and additive. R4-facing systems may use extensions, profiles, or explicit loss policy for `ingredient.role`, but those are down-conversion mitigations rather than backward-compatible base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The compatibility issue is lossy R6-to-R4 projection of new role data, not a less-breaking R6 base design needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `Medication.ingredient.role` as `0..1 CodeableConcept`.
No R4 element with id/path `Medication.ingredient.role` is present.
Binding is example strength to `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-RoleClassIngredientEntity`.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can carry the role only through an extension or non-base profile-specific convention.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a coded ingredient role. This is useful new information, but an R6 Medication using it cannot round-trip through a plain R4 Medication without loss.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6 is safe because the element is optional. R6→R4 is lossy: `ingredient.role` is an unknown element in R4, and collapsing it to `isActive` only preserves a small part of the semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When converting R6 to R4, preserve `ingredient.role` in an extension if the role affects product logic, display, or analytics. Do not assume all roles map cleanly to `isActive=true/false`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: As an optional addition, this is the least disruptive R6-side design. The compatibility burden belongs in cross-version extensions or profiles for systems that must project R6 data into R4.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Medication.ingredient.role` is an optional R6 addition. It does not invalidate any R4 Medication instance migrating forward, and the fact that populated R6 role data needs an R4 extension or loss policy is a normal downgrade issue for a new optional capability. This is useful migration awareness, not a base R4-to-R6 design problem.
keyEvidence: No R4 snapshot element with id/path `Medication.ingredient.role` is present.
R6 snapshot.element[id=Medication.ingredient.role]: `0..1 CodeableConcept`, example binding to `v3-RoleClassIngredientEntity`.
R4 and R6 both retain `Medication.ingredient.isActive` as `0..1 boolean`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use keeps Medication ingredient data important, but optional additive fields are the compatibility-preserving way to evolve mature trial-use content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: a populated R6 role is not a base R4 element, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable. The base R6 design is already additive and optional; R4 downgrade preservation belongs in extensions, profiles, or conversion policy, not in a less-breaking R6 design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly says no hard break and no base alternative is needed, but I would not treat this as a material R4-to-R6 concern.

findings.title: Medication.batch was renamed to instance and gained instance.identifier

oldState.summary: Optional batch backbone with lotNumber and expirationDate.

semanticText.definition: Information that only applies to packages (not products).

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 nested physical package/batch details under `Medication.batch`.

newState.summary: Optional instance backbone with identifier, lotNumber, and expirationDate.

semanticText.definition: Information that only applies to packages (not products).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 moves the same lot/expiration fields under `Medication.instance` and adds repeatable `instance.identifier`, typically for a serial number.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The parent short/definition and child lot/expiration definitions match closely; R6 also adds a serial/physical-instance identifier.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `batch` is absent from R6, so existing lot/expiration data must move under `instance`. R6 `instance.identifier` has no R4 base location, creating round-trip loss for serial or physical instance identifiers.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lot number, expiration date, and instance identifiers support recall, inventory, and safety workflows. Dropping or misplacing them can have operational and safety consequences.

justification.inferredGoal: Rename batch/package-specific details to a broader physical-instance concept and support serial identifiers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `batch` and add `batch.identifier`, or retain `batch` as a deprecated compatibility backbone if `instance` is introduced.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting physical-instance identifiers is reasonable, but the local definitions do not show why the existing `batch` backbone had to be removed. The old container already held package-specific lot and expiration data, and it could have been broadened or extended with an identifier. The rename therefore looks avoidable for the R4-to-R6 base design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base design would keep `Medication.batch` as the package or physical-instance details backbone, add `batch.identifier` for serial or physical-instance identifiers, and update definitions to clarify the broader meaning. If R6 also introduced `instance`, `batch` could remain deprecated with mutual-exclusion guidance, but simply extending the existing backbone would preserve R4 instances without duplicate lot/expiration paths.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps the older, narrower batch label or requires conflict rules if both backbones exist, but most R4 lot/expiration instances could remain valid.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Medication.batch` as `0..1 BackboneElement` with lotNumber and expirationDate.
R6 defines `Medication.instance` as `0..1 BackboneElement` with lotNumber and expirationDate.
R6 adds `instance.identifier` as `0..* Identifier`.

examples.examplesMd: Lot number and expiration date can usually be moved mechanically; `instance.identifier` needs an R4 extension if it must be preserved.

findings.narrativeMd: The package/batch details backbone was renamed from `batch` to `instance`. The familiar `lotNumber` and `expirationDate` children moved with it, and R6 adds a repeatable identifier for the physical instance.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `batch` is unknown in R6, so old instances with lot or expiration data fail validation until transformed. R6 `instance` is unknown in R4, and `instance.identifier` has no corresponding R4 element. Generated code must update nested component names and property paths.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `batch.lotNumber` to `instance.lotNumber` and `batch.expirationDate` to `instance.expirationDate`. For R6→R4, map those fields back to `batch` but keep `instance.identifier` in an extension if serial/physical-instance identifiers are used.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rename seems avoidable because the old backbone could have been extended. If R6 needed the broader concept of a physical instance, a transition element or extension guidance could have reduced validation breaks.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Medication.batch` moved to R6 `Medication.instance`; lot number and expiration date are essentially the same data under a new parent, with an added physical-instance identifier. Because lot and expiration data support recall, inventory, and safety workflows, a direct wire rename on FMM 3 medication content is material. The old backbone could plausibly have been retained and extended, so this rename should be revisited.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot.element[id=Medication.batch]: `0..1 BackboneElement` with `lotNumber` and `expirationDate` children.
R6 snapshot.element[id=Medication.instance]: `0..1 BackboneElement` with `lotNumber` and `expirationDate` children and no `Medication.batch` element.
R6 adds `Medication.instance.identifier` as `0..* Identifier` for the physical instance, typically a serial number.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises compatibility expectations for safety and inventory data such as lot and expiration, even though it is not normative.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `batch` is unknown in R6; R6 `instance.identifier` also has no base R4 location for reverse conversion.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have kept `batch`, broadened its definition if needed, and added `batch.identifier`. That preserves existing lot/expiration instances without duplicate paths; the main cost is retaining an older name that may be narrower than the intended R6 concept.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly identifies a high-impact hard break and a plausible less-breaking base design.

findings.title: Medication.definition adds R6-only definitional resource references

oldState.summary: No base R4 element for a formal medication definition reference.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Medication had no top-level `definition` reference.

newState.summary: Optional Reference to MedicinalProductDefinition, AdministrableProductDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, or ManufacturedItemDefinition.

semanticText.definition: A reference to a definitional resource that provides more information about this medication.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can link a Medication to product-definition resources that are not present in the R4 core package.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The optional element does not affect R4→R6 validation. It is a significant R6→R4 representability risk because the element and all listed target resource types are absent from the R4 core package.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The referenced definitional resources can carry authoritative product details. Dropping the link can degrade medication knowledge, regulatory, or product-identification workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Connect an instance-like Medication resource to richer R6 definitional product resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; `definition` is an optional R6 addition and does not invalidate R4 Medication instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Connecting Medication to richer definitional product resources is a plausible R6 expressiveness improvement, and making the reference optional is forward-compatible for R4 instances. The fact that R4 lacks the element and target resources is a downgrade concern rather than evidence of an avoidable R4-to-R6 break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because old Medication instances remain valid with respect to this optional field. R4-facing exchange may preserve populated `definition` references through extensions, external association tables, or profile-specific mappings, but those are conversion mitigations rather than base R6 alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 loss or extension/external-link handling for new product-definition references, not a forward base-design break.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `Medication.definition` as `0..1 Reference` to four definitional resource types.
No R4 element with id/path `Medication.definition` is present.
MedicinalProductDefinition, AdministrableProductDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, and ManufacturedItemDefinition are absent from the R4 core package.
All four target StructureDefinitions are present in the R6 core package.

examples.examplesMd: A plain R4 Medication cannot carry this reference as a base element and cannot point to an R4 core `MedicinalProductDefinition` resource.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `Medication.definition`, linking Medication to richer product-definition resources. This is helpful for R6 modeling but creates a substantial downgrade problem because R4 has neither the element nor those resource types in core.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6 is unaffected unless profiles require `definition`. R6→R4 loses the reference unless an extension or external association is used. Strict R4 validators reject `definition`, and the referenced resource types are not valid R4 core resources.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6→R4, preserve `definition` in an extension, external cross-reference table, or implementation-guide-specific mapping. If the referenced product-definition resource contains safety- or regulatory-critical content, do not silently drop it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is an additive R6 feature, so the main issue is not an avoidable R4→R6 break. Backward compatibility requires a cross-version representation convention because R4 cannot natively host the element or targets.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Medication.definition` is an optional R6 addition linking Medication to newer definitional product resources. It does not make any R4 Medication instance invalid in R6. A populated R6 reference cannot be represented in plain R4 because both the element and the target resources are absent there, but that is expected for new R6 expressiveness rather than an R4-to-R6 break.
keyEvidence: No R4 snapshot element with id/path `Medication.definition` is present.
R6 snapshot.element[id=Medication.definition]: `0..1 Reference` to `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `AdministrableProductDefinition`, `PackagedProductDefinition`, or `ManufacturedItemDefinition`.
Those four target StructureDefinitions are absent from the R4 core package and present in the R6 core package.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means product-definition links can matter when used, but optional additive R6 links are compatible with forward migration of R4 data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: populated R6 `definition` references and their target resources cannot be represented in base R4, but R4-to-R6 instances are unaffected.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable. No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4 compatibility because the field is optional and additive; downgrade handling requires extension or external-link policy.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing downgrade facts and Not applicable alternative are right, but I would classify the finding as no R4-to-R6 problem rather than a medium-impact break.

findings.title: Medication.status keeps the same required codes but changes code definitions toward record currency

oldState.summary: Optional modifier code with required binding to medication-status|4.0.1.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: The medication is available for use.
changedCodes.newMeaning: The medication record is current and is appropriate for reference in new instances.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Meaning shifted from medication availability to medication-record currency/reference suitability.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The code set remained active/inactive/entered-in-error, but definitions changed.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 status described whether the medication itself was available for use.

newState.summary: Optional modifier code with required binding to medication-status|6.0.0-ballot4; same three codes with changed definitions.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: The medication is available for use.
changedCodes.newMeaning: The medication record is current and is appropriate for reference in new instances.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Semantics now emphasize the medication record's current/reference status.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: The medication is not available for use.
changedCodes.newMeaning: The medication record is not current and is not appropriate for reference in new instances.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Semantics now emphasize record currency rather than product availability.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: The medication was entered in error.
changedCodes.newMeaning: The medication record was created erroneously and is not appropriate for reference in new instances.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Semantics now emphasize erroneous record creation and reference suitability.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Code membership appears unchanged from local CodeSystem concepts and ConceptMap mappings, but full terminology expansion was not performed.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 status describes whether the medication record is current and appropriate for reference in new instances.

facts.note: Local CodeSystem concepts show no added or removed codes.

facts.oldValue: The medication is available for use.
facts.newValue: The medication record is current and is appropriate for reference in new instances.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The same literal codes should validate in both versions, so this is not a hard instance break. The risk is semantic: software that interprets `active` as product availability may behave incorrectly if R6 expects record currency/reference suitability. Because `status` is a modifier, consumers are already expected to account for its meaning.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Medication status can control whether a medication definition is selectable, displayed, or used in new orders. Misinterpreting record status as market availability, or vice versa, can affect order/catalog behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify status as a statement about the Medication record's currentness and suitability for reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old availability-oriented code meanings and add a separate record-currency/status element or terminology distinction for the R6 concept.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying `Medication.status` as record currentness and suitability for reference is a reasonable goal, and the same code literals continue to validate, so there is no raw instance break. However, changing required-code definitions under stable codes can surprise business logic that treated status as medication availability. A less-breaking design exists, but it would add a separate concept or terminology layer and make status modeling more complex, so the current approach is probably justified but not fully unavoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would preserve the R4 code definitions for `active`, `inactive`, and `entered-in-error` and introduce a distinct element or code system for record currency/reference suitability. That would better protect existing runtime semantics, but it would require implementations to manage two related status dimensions and would not provide the same simple single modifier status in base R6. Documentation or ConceptMaps alone would be mitigation, not a base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids silent semantic reuse of the same codes, but adds terminology/model complexity and may preserve ambiguity between product availability and record currentness.

evidence.detail: R4 binds `Medication.status` required to `medication-status|4.0.1`.
R6 binds `Medication.status` required to `medication-status|6.0.0-ballot4`.
R4 `active` definition is availability-oriented; R6 `active` definition is record-current/reference-oriented.
Both R4 and R6 canonical maps still map active/inactive/entered-in-error to equivalent resource-status concepts.

examples.examplesMd: The example remains structurally valid; the issue is that a rule interpreting `active` as product availability may need review under R6 semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: `Medication.status` did not change codes or cardinality, but the code definitions changed materially. R4 talked about whether the medication is available for use; R6 talks about whether the medication record is current and appropriate for reference in new instances.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not old-valid/new-invalid at the JSON level because the same codes remain in the required value set. It is still a compatibility risk for validators with terminology displays/definitions, enum documentation, decision-support rules, and catalog selection logic that treat status as real-world product availability.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review all business logic attached to `Medication.status`, especially filters for active formularies, orderable products, and catalog maintenance. If product market availability is needed separately from record currentness, do not rely solely on R6 `Medication.status` without a profile, extension, or linked product-definition data.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: If the change is intended as clarification, stronger narrative migration notes would make it safer. If it is a normative semantic shift, preserving the old concept or adding a distinct element/code system could have reduced ambiguity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Full terminology expansion was not required to see the three local codes, but official narrative/change notes would improve confidence about intent.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The literal status codes and required binding remain the same, but local CodeSystem definitions moved from medication availability wording to medication-record currentness/reference wording. That could affect business rules that treat `active` as availability, especially because `status` is a modifier. However, the Medication element definition and comment remain largely availability/local-drug-record oriented, so the evidence does not prove whether R6 intended a normative semantic shift or a clarification of the existing local-record concept. Official rationale or terminology governance notes are needed.
keyEvidence: R4 and R6 `Medication.status` are both `0..1 code`, `isModifier=true`, with required binding to versioned `medication-status` ValueSets.
R4 CodeSystem `active` definition: `The medication is available for use.` R6 definition: `The medication record is current and is appropriate for reference in new instances.`
The R6 StructureDefinition `Medication.status` definition/comment still says the status indicates if the medication is in active use in a local drug database or inventory.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises concern for a modifier status on a central Medication resource, but the ambiguity between clarification and semantic change prevents a firmer judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the same instances validate, but runtime rules or enum documentation that attach behavior to `active`/`inactive` may interpret the codes differently.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Unknown or Partial. If R6 truly changed the concept, a separate record-currentness element or code system would be less surprising but would add model complexity; if this is only clarification, no less-breaking design is needed.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly spots a semantic risk and partial alternative, but I would not accept its confidence/proportionality conclusion without official intent evidence.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 StructureDefinition exists at the expected path and preserves the canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Medication`, id/name/type `Medication`, kind `resource`, base `DomainResource`, derivation `specialization`, and `abstract=false`. The conformance status change is noted separately as non-breaking.

No local semantically matched Medication element has a minimum cardinality increase or maximum cardinality decrease. The material breaks are removals/renames, type-domain changes, and added optional elements. `ingredient.item` remains `1..1`; most other local elements remain optional.

No Medication-specific invariants were found in the local differential. Constraint differences observed on root/base and extension elements are inherited from `DomainResource`, `Element`, or `Extension` and are out of scope for this Medication report.
No local Medication element added, removed, or changed a fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraint.
No local Medication element introduced material minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limits in the compared StructureDefinitions.

The local modifier status of `Medication.status` remains `isModifier=true`; other local reported structural changes did not introduce a new modifier element. Inherited modifier-extension behavior is out of scope.
No local slicing or discriminator changes were identified on Medication elements in either StructureDefinition.

Binding strengths on exact surviving local elements did not tighten except for new elements/choice forms reported elsewhere. `Medication.status` semantic/code-definition changes and example/preferred ValueSet changes are reported; full terminology expansions were not performed.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical URL, id, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are unchanged. The conformance-resource `status` affects maturity/governance, not instance wire format.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance processes may treat R6 Medication as more mature, but parsers do not migrate instance data because of this field alone.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Resource definition and ingredient comments now emphasize ingredients and compounded products
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The root definition text was expanded to mention ingredients, and `Medication.ingredient` comments add guidance about fully specified products and compounded products. These are narrative/semantic clarifications rather than validator-enforced cardinality or type changes beyond findings already reported.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementation guides may use the new comments to guide when ingredients should be populated even when `Medication.code` is fully specified.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Medication.code definition adds guidance that code.text can carry the medication name
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element remains optional `CodeableConcept` with example binding to `medication-codes`; the added text broadens/explains use of `CodeableConcept.text` rather than invalidating old instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Display/name extraction code should consider `Medication.code.text`, even when coding displays differ.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Example SNOMED value-set filters changed for medication codes and form codes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The affected bindings are example strength, so base validation does not reject codes outside the examples. Local ValueSet compose definitions changed from R4 SNOMED filters `410942007`, `373873005`, `106181007` to R6 `763158003` for medication codes, and from `421967003` to `736542009` for form codes.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology-aware implementations, picklists, and QA rules that use the example value sets should re-evaluate expansions against the R6 SNOMED filters.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Several observed differences are inherited base-artifact changes, including root `dom-*` constraint expression metadata, `ele-1`/extension constraint metadata, base field behavior such as `language`, and inherited extension/modifierExtension details. Per scope instructions, those are excluded from Medication findings.

Medication.ingredient.item now depends on CodeableReference. The datatype's own cross-version behavior and serializer/codegen implications should be handled by the CodeableReference/datatype analysis.
R6 Medication can reference R6-only definitional/product resources from `Medication.definition` and `Medication.ingredient.item`. Downgrade strategy depends on those resources' own R4/R6 analyses.
Local compose and CodeSystem comparisons identified binding/value-set changes, but full expansions and edition-specific terminology effects require a terminology analysis.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 narrative diff, ballot reconciliation note, or Jira/change proposal was used. The report relies on local package artifacts and inferred matching between removed and added elements.
